name: scikit-image
summary: scikit-image allows AI only for narrow, easily reviewable work: fixing trivial bugs, mechanical edits and infrastructure code, with the AI use declared, an Assisted-by commit tag, and the human author responsible for understanding and copyright. AI-written novel code, tests, pull request descriptions, issue/PR comments and answers to reviewers are not allowed.

evidence.quote: Disclose all generative tools (AI, LLMs, agents) that you used, see our AI Policy for details.
To preserve our culture of collaboration, we (the human maintainers) need to know that you (the human author) fully understand the code you have submitted, and its implications for the code-base.
For exploring the codebase, for iterating on hand-written code, and for fixing trivial bugs.
Always declare tool usage: say specifically what part of the task you used AI for in the PR description.

AI-generated code must be trivial to review: the reviewer must be able to review the AI-generated code with little background in image-processing or experience working on the code-base, and see that the changes are correct.

You must take responsibility for copyright of the AI-generated code; the simplest and best way to do this, is to make sure the code changes are trivial, in the sense that they cannot reasonably be done differently to solve the given problem.
Expect the team to ask questions about your work - and you must answer these questions yourself, without deferring to AI.
To automate mechanical tasks. E.g., if you discover that you need to add a decorator across the code-base.
For infrastructure code, such as CI, as long as the changes are easy to review.
If you want to make use of LLMs in a significant way and have your contributions reviewed, safest is to check in with us first to discuss your strategy.
Creating novel code (algorithmic additions, writing tests, etc.).[1]
Note that tests, specifically, are rarely trivial [1].
As far as possible, separate AI-generated code from human-generated code with individual commits.
Tag AI commits with an Assisted-by: tag as recommended by the Linux kernel.
Writing pull request descriptions, or commenting on issues or PRs.
Write PR descriptions and comments by hand. If you do quote AI text, do so sparingly, and indicate where you’re doing so, e.g. by writing :robot: _AI text below_ :robot:.
Expect the team to ask questions about your work - and you must answer these questions yourself, without deferring to AI.

Core maintainers may use their own judgment on when and how to use AI, including for tasks outside the “how you may use AI” list above. They must still follow the requirements section: declaring tool usage, tagging commits, etc.
